subject: Cascade Health — data transfer controls, DPA annex and technical clarifications
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@cascadehealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal.ops@cascadehealth.com, security@cascadehealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RFI — international transfer controls / DPA annex questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — Cascade Health is evaluating Redwood for inference in several clinical workflows. Our procurement and legal teams have a short set of technical questions to confirm before we proceed to contracting. Can you please provide consolidated answers and any supporting artifacts (SOC 2, subprocessor list, DPA Annex template, and a brief technical map) by COB tomorrow if possible? Below are the specific items we need answered for our privacy assessment: 

1) Cross-border transfers: Do you rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or the new DPF framework for EU->US transfers? If both, which do you default to and how do you decide routing for customer data?

2) DPA Annex: Please provide your standard DPA Annex text (including routing, subprocessors, and data export clauses). Will you accept customer redlines for controller-to-processor clauses and do you have a list of mandatory non-negotiables?

3) Subprocessors & residency: Current list of subprocessors (for processing, storage, monitoring). Can we get an export-friendly CSV? For customers requiring EU-only processing, what deployment options exist (VPC, dedicated, on-prem)?

4) Key management and encryption: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? For hosted deployments, where are keys stored and who has administrative access?

5) Logs & retention: What categories of logs (request/response bodies, full-text logs, tokens) are retained by default, for how long, and what are the options to shorten retention or disable certain logs?

6) Technical safeguards & caching: Does your inference runtime perform prefix caching / KV cache that could persist user data? How can customers control caching behavior for regulated workloads?

Bonus: any attestation documents you can share (SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summary, DPF technical mapping) would be very helpful.

If there's a better template you prefer we provide (e.g., a completed questionnaire), let me know and I can send it. Thanks — Emily

--
Emily Carter
Head of Vendor Risk, Cascade Health
emily.carter@cascadehealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial RFI — international transfer controls / DPA annex questions

Quick draft answers and attachments checklist for the external reply: 

A) Cross-border transfers:
- We default to EU SCCs (2021 SCCs) for controller-to-processor flows. For customers who require DPF/adequacy mapping we provide a DPF Technical Safeguards Map that documents routing, supplemental measures, and lawful-basis modeling. Routing is policy-driven: customers can require region-only routing (Dedicated/Private) or allow hosted with SCCs + supplemental controls.

B) DPA Annex & redlines: 
- Attached: DPA_Annex_Template_Redwood_v1.docx (standard clauses). We accept customer redlines on most commercial and processing clauses; non-negotiables are limited to our security baseline claims (e.g., we cannot remove our right to subprocessor chaining with notice). Recommend legal to review but we can provide a marked-up sample.

C) Subprocessors & residency: 
- Subprocessors_List_2026-04-03.csv will include cloud providers, monitoring vendors, and analytics processors. For EU-only residency: Dedicated EU capacity or Private (VPC/On-prem) is the supported option — estimated delivery ~6–10 weeks depending on capacity and contract.

D) KMS & keys: 
- We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS, and HSM-backed key escrow for Private deployments. For hosted customers who opt for Redwood-managed keys, keys are stored in our KMS with strict role-based access; key access logs are captured and available in audit exports.

E) Logs & retention: 
- Default retention: 90 days for request metadata and 30 days for minimally retained response traces used for quality monitoring. Customers can request shorter retention or opt-out of storing full request/response bodies for regulated workloads; this is stated in the annex as a configuration option. Permanent deletion processes and verification logs are available for Dedicated/Private deployments.

F) Caching & runtime safeguards: 
- The runtime uses per-request KV caching and optional prefix caching to reduce token costs. For regulated customers caching can be disabled per-model or per-route; customers can also configure automatic cache eviction and ensure no raw PII is cached by enabling input scrubbing (we provide SDK helpers).

Attachments we should include in external reply: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf (redacted), DPA_Annex_Template_Redwood_v1.docx, Subprocessors_List_2026-04-03.csv, DPF_Technical_Safeguards_Map.pdf.

I'll pull redacted SOC2 and the subprocessors list now. Kim, once you confirm the DPA annex I'll hand to Jonas for review.

—Monica

Hi Emily,

Thanks — please find consolidated answers below and four artifacts attached. If you’d prefer a pre-filled vendor questionnaire instead of narrative answers, we can complete that as well.

Summary answers (high level):
1) Cross-border transfers: Redwood defaults to the 2021 EU Standard Contractual Clauses for EU->US transfers. For customers that request DPF mapping or additional supplemental measures we provide a documented DPF Technical Safeguards Map (attached) and will work with you to implement any required routing/policy controls. Hosted customers can use SCCs + supplemental controls; EU-only processing is supported via Dedicated EU capacity or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.

2) DPA Annex: Attached is our standard DPA Annex template (DPA_Annex_Template_Redwood_v1.docx). We accept customer redlines on most clauses. Mandatory baseline clauses we require relate to our security baseline (e.g., ability to use subprocessors with notice, minimal logging for incident response). If there are specific clauses Cascade cannot accept, flag them and we’ll escalate to legal for exceptions.

3) Subprocessors & residency: Attached is a current exportable subprocessors CSV (Subprocessors_List_2026-04-03.csv). It includes cloud infra, observability, and telemetry vendors. For strict residency requirements we recommend Dedicated EU or Private deployment; lead times vary by contract and capacity — we can provide firm timelines once requirements are finalized.

4) Key management & encryption: We support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for hosted and Dedicated, and HSM-backed options for Private deployments. Logs of key use are retained in audit exports; administrative access is limited to authorized personnel and logged.

5) Logs & retention: Our default policy is 90 days for request metadata and 30 days for transient response traces used for quality monitoring. Customers can request amendments (shorter retention, disable response-body retention) and these options are documented in the DPA Annex. For Dedicated/Private we provide configurable retention and deletion verification processes.

6) Caching & runtime safeguards: The inference runtime supports KV and prefix caching to optimize latency and cost. For regulated workloads customers may disable caching per-route or enable automatic scrubbing to remove PII before cache insertion. We provide SDK-level helpers and abort hooks to assist integration.

Attached artifacts (redacted where required):
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf (SOC 2 Type II summary with redactions for sensitive controls)
- DPA_Annex_Template_Redwood_v1.docx (standard annex text, with notes on configurable fields)
- Subprocessors_List_2026-04-03.csv (exportable list of subprocessors and roles)
- DPF_Technical_Safeguards_Map.pdf (mapping of supplemental measures for DPF adequacy requests)

Next steps: if Cascade would like, we can (1) run a short 30–45 minute technical walk-through of the DPF map and key management options, (2) provide a marked DPA annex with any proposed Cascade redlines, and (3) schedule legal-to-legal call to accelerate contracting.

Let me know which you prefer and I’ll coordinate.

Best,
